add.issue.name: The diff composer's three buttons read as three unrelated controls

edit.description.md:
Reported from the comment-on-code composer: cancel / File ticket / Comment don't look like one set.

Three faults, all in `SelectionComposer` + `Button`:

- `primary`'s fill is `GUI_THEME.tertiary` — the exact colour of the composer's own ground — so "Comment" loses its body and reads as bold text, while "File ticket" next to it is a bordered box.
- Each variant carries its own padding (ghost 3/6, default 5/9, primary 6/12), so the three sit at three different heights in one row.
- Labels are Title Case; every other button in the GUI is lowercase ("cancel", "save", "comment", "close issue").

Fix so the row reads as one set with a clear hierarchy, without changing how `primary` looks on the panel/modal grounds it already sits on.

add.issue.name: The topbar spells out the sync state; the dot alone can carry it

edit.description.md:
Drop the "synced" / "syncing…" / "sync failed" word from the header and keep the coloured dot, which already says the same thing.

- The full state goes in the dot's `title`, so TooltipLayer shows it on hover (and a failure's git output keeps going there, as it does today).
- The dot is 4px and effectively unhoverable, so it gets a ghost-button-sized hit area around it.

Parked: the dot could be a real button that syncs on click — `send('sync', {})` already exists for the palette. Not done here; a click in the topbar that pushes and pulls is the user's call, not a styling change.

add.issue.name: The window funnel belongs beside Zoom, not at the far end of the row

edit.description.md:
`SpotlightToggle` (narrow board to the timeline window) sits last on the scrubber row, past the series pickers and the text filter. It narrows the board to the window the period buttons and Zoom select, so it belongs immediately right of Zoom — same subject, one group.

Move it there in both the wide row and the `narrow` variant (right of `ScopeSelect`), and rewrite the comment that currently argues for the old position.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: 9cd757e4 (PR #368).

`primary` no longer paints itself `GUI_THEME.tertiary` — a surface colour that happened to be this composer's own ground — but `GUI_THEME.raised`, a white wash one step past `hover`, so it reads as raised wherever it sits. Padding now belongs to the box, not the variant: everything that draws one shares `5px 9px`, `ghost` keeps its tighter inline figure, and `dense` is unchanged.

Applied to the other action rows too, so the rule holds: the confirming button in the comment composer, the comment editor and the description editor is `primary`, and the description editor's `cancel` now comes first like every other row. Labels lowercased — the composer's `File ticket` was Title Case against the `file ticket` confirm in the modal it opens.

The rule is written on the `variant` prop rather than at the call sites.
add.issue.comment.author: SM58B810Y2CMRKX2WZCHD9DRXJ

add.issue.name: The LIVE banner sits inside the board; it belongs at the top of the window

edit.description.md:
Follow-up to `9V0Y58E`, from jola: the following banner reads as part of the board rather than as a statement about the whole app.

It is rendered inside `<main>`, so it starts past the log panel and sits below the topbar and the timeline. Move it to the top of the page — the first thing in the chrome band, above the header, full window width — and keep it at full strength while a movie dims the rest of that band, the way the topbar already is.

The 2px accent rule stays on top, where it becomes the window's own live edge; the comment in `FollowBanner` that explains it as a seam against the chrome above needs rewriting with it.

add.issue.name: A long log line runs over the VIEW chip instead of being cut off behind it

edit.description.md:
Reported by jola: on a row with a long label, the hover VIEW affordance is obscured by the line's own text.

The chip (`LOG_ARROW_CLASS`) is `position: absolute` with an opaque ground, and its comment says a long line is cut off behind it. It is not: the chip is the first child of the scroll pane and every `.epiq-log-line` is `position: relative`, so the rows are positioned siblings later in the DOM and paint above it. The chip only shows at all because a row's own ground is transparent or a wash.

Fix the paint order and check the claim the comment makes actually holds.

add.issue.name: The Now mark stays lit on the track while a movie plays

edit.description.md:
Reported by jola: the snap-back control is on the chart during playback, where it should not be.

`standDown` takes the scrubber's pointer events away and dims its control row to 0.3, but the chart below keeps its own brightness — so `ReturnToNowButton`, which is a filled accent box, is the one thing still lit on a bar that has stood down, and it is inert. The player's own ✕ is what leaves a movie.

Hide it while a movie is up, and say so where the button's "only while the board is parked" rule is written.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: 3deda23f (PR #371).

The banner is now the first child of the chrome band — full window width, above the Header, with its 2px accent rule along the window's own top edge — and outside the theatre-dim wrapper, so it stays at full strength while a movie dims the rest of that band.

`pointerEvents: 'none'` is untouched, so "click anywhere to opt out" still reaches what is behind it; the band it now sits in is not exempt from the capture listener either, so a click there still leaves following.

Both comments that described the old placement were rewritten with it.
add.issue.comment.author: SM58B810Y2CMRKX2WZCHD9DRXJ

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: 2ddbbc4e (PR #372).

Paint order, as diagnosed: the chip is the first child of the scroll pane and every `.epiq-log-line` is `position: relative`, so the rows are positioned siblings later in the DOM and painted over the chip's opaque ground. `z-index: 1` gives it a layer of its own, and the comment now says why it needs one rather than only that the ground is opaque.

Regression test in `event-log.pw.ts`, verified red without the fix — the computed `z-index` was `auto`.
add.issue.comment.author: SM58B810Y2CMRKX2WZCHD9DRXJ

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: 75a7e4c6 (PR #373).

`ReturnToNowButton` is no longer rendered while `standDown` is on. The rule lives in `ScrubberLayout`, next to the stand-down it belongs to, rather than inside the button — the button's own "only while the board is parked" comment points at it.

Regression test in `theatre.pw.ts`, verified red without the fix: no Now during playback, and it returns once the player is gone and the board is parked in the past.
